metadata.description: A United Press newspaper article reports that Dr. Alfred H. Upham, president of Miami University in Oxford, Ohio, Mrs. Upham, and their daughter Peggy Lou were among passengers rescued from the liner President Hoover after it grounded on a reef off Formosa. The article states that the Uphams had left Oxford on November 17 for a tour of the orient and that their itinerary included a two-week visit to Yokohama.
metadata.title: Newspaper article on Dr. Upham and family aboard the President Hoover, 11 December 1937
metadata.transcript:
[page 1]
[illegible]

Dr. [Doctor] Upham, Wife and Daughter Taken From Hoover Liner

By the United Press.

Dr. [Doctor] Alfred H. Upham, president of Miami University, Oxford, O. [Ohio], Mrs. [Missus] Upham and their daughter, Peggy Lou, 26, were among 503 passengers rescued Saturday from the liner President Hoover, aground on a reef off Formosa, in the Pacific, 400 miles south of Japan.

Dr. [Doctor] Upham, enjoying his first vacation in 10 years, had been on a tour of the orient.

The Uphams left Oxford Nov. [November] 17, and were to return in mid-April.

The family was believed safe, although reports from the stricken liner said the ship's physician, Dr. [Doctor] Kenneth Park, had set up an emergency hospital on Hoishoto Island, where the passengers were taken. It was assumed several passengers were suffering from exposure.

Friends and relatives of Dr. [Doctor] and Mrs. [Missus] Upham at Oxford expressed hope today that the Uphams were not aboard the liner. Dr. [Doctor] Upham's itinerary called for a two-week visit to Yokohama [Yokohama, Japan]. The last word heard from him was that he had landed safely at Yokohama [Yokohama, Japan], Dec. [December] 6. It is believed, however, Dr. [Doctor] Upham may have changed his mind due to unsettled conditions in the Orient, and sailed on the President Hoover.

Seas Are Heavy

Radio advices indicated heavy seas had made difficult the ferrying of the 503 passengers and salvage of President Hoover, which was standing by.

The President Hoover's sister ship, the President McKinley, racing to the scene under full steam, was expected to arrive at dusk. It was believed the ship's cargo would have to be jettisoned before it could be refloated.

The liner was aground about 30 miles off Formosa, the chief island of the group. One of her last messages asked for all possible salvage aid. Presumably her crew of 330 remained aboard. Capt. [Captain] George Yardley, commander of the liner, reported that there was no immediate danger.

(Continued on Page 2, Col. 8)

MIAMI UNIVERSITY LIBRARY
